label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. The harness withheld recent_deploys, service_health: each call to it got the error its source gives when it does not answer, and never reached that source (an outage simulated for this case; the stack itself was not touched). Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 10 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.right_answer: The ledger consumer books a second time every webhook the provider sends again: its dedupe is gone (fault 1's recorded cause, which a deploy brought). Docker did not answer the two tools that read it, so the deploy list and the containers' health could not be read: a right diagnosis says what it could not check, and claims no deploy it has no evidence for. Rolling the ledger consumer back still fits the remedy: code plans a rollback from the deploy log, not from the tools.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer restarted at about 06:27:40 in 'naive' mode, where it no longer skips events it has already booked. The provider re-sends webhooks, and the receiver queues each retry as a new Kafka message. Before the restart the ledger caught these duplicates ('already processed'). Since the restart, duplicates are booked again, so payment.succeeded and refund.succeeded events are posted 2 or 3 times. That fails posted_exactly_once and leaves the ledger $461.00 ahead of the provider. The ledger stays balanced because each duplicate is a balanced entry. Payments and refunds still match the provider because payment-confirmer handles duplicates correctly. Not confirmed: recent_deploys failed twice with a Docker timeout, so I could not see the LEDGER_HANDLER setting or what the previous deploy ran. The 'naive' mode comes from one log line, and its timing matches the first double post I traced.

evidence.shows: Two invariants fail: posted_exactly_once (7 events posted 2-3 times) and matches_provider (ledger +$461.00). ledger_balanced, payments_match_provider and refunds_match_provider pass, so the fault is in ledger booking only.
evt_000251 was posted twice by ledger-consumer, from Kafka offsets 2＠73 (06:27:39.595) and 2＠76 (06:27:40.329), under two different trace ids.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000251 twice (offsets 73 and 76), about 0.5s apart. This fits a provider retry that the receiver does not deduplicate, so deduplication has to happen in the consumers.
Ledger outcomes: 395 posted, 14 already_processed. payment-confirmer shows 363 already_confirmed and 36 refund_already_confirmed, so it handles duplicates correctly.

Up to 06:27:37 the ledger logged 'already processed' for duplicates, so its dedup worked. Then it logged 'partitions revoked', 'ledger consumer stopped' (06:27:39.7) and 'ledger consumer starting' with mode 'naive' (06:27:40.26). The second post of evt_000251 came right after that restart.
recent_deploys failed again with a Docker timeout (as in c2), so the settings change and the rollback target could not be checked.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, which should restore idempotent handling. Before approving, check recent_deploys once Docker responds, to confirm the latest deploy is the one that set 'naive'. A rollback only stops new double postings and repairs nothing. The existing duplicates need a separate data repair, which no listed action covers: reverse the extra ledger transactions (e.g. 255, 265, 272, 273, 297, plus the extra ones for evt_000298 and evt_000308), then rerun money_check. The check showed only 5 of its 7 and 8 findings, so I have not identified every duplicate.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated. Kafka events wait in the topic and the lag clears after the restart. payment-confirmer, webhook-receiver and payments-api are not touched. If the previous deploy was not the one that set 'naive', the rollback may restore the wrong settings. Bookings already made stay wrong.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, recreate ledger-consumer with the settings it has now (mode 'naive', per the c6 log), watch the ledger outcomes in klaxon_consumer_events_total, and rerun money_check with wait=true to see whether new duplicates appear.
